The move expands an investigation that was previously focused on Israel's far-right national security minister, Itamar Ben-Gvir.

The case concerns suspected torture, kidnapping, personal injury, robbery and damage when Israeli forces intercepted small fleets of ​boats headed towards Gaza in 2025 and 2026, the Rome prosecutors' office said in a ​statement.

Investigators opened the probe after complaints from 50 Italian citizens who were detained ⁠by Israeli authorities following two Global Sumud Flotilla missions in September to October 2025 and April ​to May 2026.

Prosecutors said activists detained after the first mission had reported beatings, injuries, death threats, insults and accusations of terrorism.

Activists involved in the ​second mission reported even harsher treatment, including beatings in the dark, the use of tasers and ​rubber bullets, the statement said.

Under ​Italian law, crimes ⁠committed abroad against Italian citizens can be prosecuted in Rome.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] UN says West Bank olive harvest settler attacks surpass 2025 figure
item.description:
UN says West Bank olive harvest settler attacks surpass 2025 figure

The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (Ocha) reports that the number of settler attacks in the West Bank affecting the olive harvest season has already exceeded last year’s number.

So far this year, nearly 200 settler attacks linked to the olive harvest have caused casualties or property damage, Ocha said in a statement. That is more than the 185 incidents recorded during the entire 2025 season.

This year’s attacks have killed one Palestinian, injured more than 120 others, and damaged over 2,500 trees or saplings. About 80 per cent of these incidents took place in the past two weeks, with many communities starting to pick olives early to reduce the risks, the statement read.

Humanitarian partners have provided pickers with equipment and other agricultural supplies. They are also monitoring restrictions imposed by the Israeli authorities on access to groves close to settlements and behind the 712-kilometre-long Barrier, and providing legal support.

"In Gaza, humanitarian partners say the destruction of olive groves, restricted access to farmland – particularly beyond the “Yellow Line” – and restrictions on the entry of agricultural supplies, engine oil and spare parts are severely limiting cultivation and harvesting, as well as the operation of the few remaining olive presses," the statement said.

UKMTO says most vessels don't report Hormuz attacks

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) has said it was struggling to establish the true number of attacks in the Strait of Hormuz because most vessels attacked were refusing to report incidents to the agency.

In its 'Voluntary Reporting Area Weekly Overview', the maritime security watchdog said that reports received through other sources could not always be verified. It also said that US-reported facilitated transit figures could not be independently verified.

Combined inbound and outbound transits through the Strait of Hormuz remained about 70 percent below pre-war levels, it said.

The UKMTO added that of the 12 vessels struck during its latest weekly reporting period--10 in Hormuz and one each in the Gulf and the Gulf of Oman--six continued their journeys or reached port, one was lost, and two were disabled or not under command.

Damage or outcomes remained unconfirmed in three cases, according to the report.

item.description:
Most minors subjected to solitary confinement in Israeli prisons Palestinians, report says

More than half of the minors held in Israeli prisons in 2025 were placed in solitary confinement at least once, including five boys aged 13 to 14, with the vast majority of the children being Palestinians, Haaretz reported, citing data obtained by two Israeli human rights organisations.

Of 635 minors held in prison, 351 were placed in solitary confinement, usually for seven consecutive days and sometimes for up to two weeks, according to the data obtained through a freedom of information request by the Public Committee Against Torture in Israel and Parents Against Child Detention.

The Israel Prison Service said 92% of the minors placed in isolation had not been sentenced. This included 176 held pending the conclusion of legal proceedings and 115 detained without trial under Shin Bet orders in administrative detention.

The data showed that solitary confinement was imposed 666 times, with 154 minors isolated more than once, including 42 who were placed in isolation between four and eight times.

Titi Carmel, director of Parents Against Child Detention, told Haaretz that the recurring use of solitary confinement was particularly concerning because of its potential harm to children.

Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian has called the destruction of ecosystems caused by the "wars of aggression" an act of "ecocide", urging the international community to establish effective and enforceable mechanisms to protect biodiversity during armed conflicts.

Pezeshkian described the environmental devastation caused by the wars in the region, including in Gaza, as “ecocide” that must be condemned, adding that pollution and ecological damage transcend national borders, Tasnim reported.

"War not only kills people and destroys economic infrastructure but also burns forests, damages wetlands, contaminates soil, threatens water resources and destroys wildlife habitats.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure 'worrying' for Pakistan's outlook, minister says
item.description:
Attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure 'worrying' for Pakistan's outlook, minister says

Pakistan's finance minister said on Saturday the country had so far withstood the shock from skyrocketing energy prices due to the Iran war, but that attacks on infrastructure in Saudi Arabia and other Gulf countries were "worrying" for the country's longer-term economic outlook.

In an interview on the sidelines of the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Muhammad Aurangzeb told AFP said the South Asian country had procured enough energy supplies to last through November, and was now planning for the winter months, when household needs typically spike.

"The first-order impact has been negotiated well by Pakistan," he said.

"We've had no shortage, no queues at the gas stations, and no law and order situation, which at times we have seen in some of the countries."

He added that unless the government saw "an absolute dire need", it would not be procuring spot cargoes on the LNG front, which tend to be far more expensive than previously contracted shipments.

Since the United States and ally Israel launched the war on Iran in February, global energy prices have surged as Tehran's retaliatory action has targeted Washington's Gulf allies and curtailed oil and gas supplies.

With Yemen's civil war flaring back to life as well, the Houthis there have repeatedly attacked Saudi infrastructure, including energy facilities and airports, in recent days.

Aurangzeb expressed alarm at the escalation, saying damage to such sites would delay a return to economic normalcy.

"What is now (the) worrying part of it is when the energy infrastructure starts getting hit," he said.

"I, to be very honest, I don't know where that would go. But one thing is very clear: that if the infrastructure continues to get hit, the return to normalcy, even if things subside, will take longer."

Report by AFP

item.description:
Israeli forces arrest two Palestinians, settlers open fire at farmers in West Bank

Separately, Wafa reported that Israeli forces arrested two Palestinian men during dawn raids in Nablus and the nearby village of Tal.

item.title: [World news | The Guardian] ‘Austerity is inevitably painful’: How Michael Gove justifies his politics | Radical Thinking with Aditya Chakrabortty – podcast
item.description:
For more than three decades, Michael Gove has been a leading figure in British Conservatism. As a journalist, government minister and now editor of the Tory bible, the Spectator, he has helped shape the right even as it has moved further rightwards. In the latest episode of Radical Thinking, Gove joins Aditya Chakrabortty to discuss the future of the right, his record on Brexit and austerity, and the Spectator’s position on Islam

Watch the full episode with Michael Gove here.

Aditya’s suggested reading:

To read the fruits of Michael Gove’s dalliance with the Marxism Today gang, look up his essay in a 1998 collection called The Moderniser’s Dilemma: Radical Politics in the Age of Blair

For slalom ride through Michael Gove’s years in power, read The Demented Dalek by the historian Richard J Evans in the London Review of Books

To learn more on what’s become of the British right, there’s a column by me for the Guardian

Just why the most successful political party is now failing is analysed in-depth by Phil Burton-Cartledge in his book The Party’s Over: The Rise and Fall of the Conservatives from Thatcher to Sunak

Phil also writes a very good blog on British politics, which keeps a close eye on how each party is trying to marshall a coalition of voters. Here he is on Kemi Badenoch

Geoffrey Wheatcroft does an entertaining short narrative in Bloody Panico!:

or, Whatever Happened to The Tory Party

For more on the economics of the Cameron years, this paper is acute on how the Tories failed to move the UK away from being a country of renters towards a country of makers. Two of its authors will join us for a podcast later in the series.

And if you want to read how Brexit may have cost the UK 8% of GDP, there’s this paper based on data from the Bank of England

Finally, on the Spectator read Nesrine Malik’s recent column in The Guardian

Why has Britain’s oldest political magazine become such a rabid cheerleader for Islamophobia?

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Morning update
item.description:
Morning update


Good Morning Middle East Eye readers,

If you are just joining us, here are key developments from across the region and beyond:

* Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) navy has said a supertanker carrying more than 2 million barrels of crude oil struck a sea mine while attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz through a “prohibited” area.

* US President Donald Trump says the US Navy is carrying out an effective blockade of Iran and that no Iranian ship has been able to cross the Strait of Hormuz.

* Yemen’s government-aligned forces say 378 Houthi fighters have been killed or wounded in ground clashes and air attacks in Taiz governorate, while the Saudi-led coalition forces claimed two Houthi ballistic missile launchers were destroyed in Yemen’s northern Saada governorate.

*The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) has said that a tanker has been struck by an unknown projectile 68 nautical miles northeast of Al Jubail, Saudi Arabia, on Friday.

* Israeli settlers opened fire at and attacked Palestinian farmers in the village of Deir Jarir, east of Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, Al Jazeera reported.

*The United Kingdom's Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office has advised British citizens against all but essential travel to all of  Saudi Arabia.

* Pakistan finance minister says attacks on infrastructure in Saudi Arabia and other Gulf countries were "worrying" for the country's longer-term economic outlook.

* Houthi shelling and sniper fire killed a woman and injured five civilians, including a woman and a young girl, in the Sabir al-Mawadim district southeast of Taiz, Al Jazeera reported, citing Yemeni media report.

* Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian has called the destruction of ecosystems caused by the "wars of aggression" an act of "ecocide", urging the international community to establish effective and enforceable mechanisms to protect biodiversity during armed conflicts.

* Three US lawmakers have called on the Trump administration to hold Israeli settlers accountable after an attack on Washington Post photographer Heidi Levine and Palestinian villagers in the occupied West Bank. 

* More than half of the minors held in Israeli prisons in 2025 were placed in solitary confinement at least once, including five boys aged 13 to 14, with the vast majority of the children being Palestinians

* The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) has said it was struggling to establish the true number of attacks in the Strait of Hormuz because most vessels attacked were refusing to report incidents to the agency.

* Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has said the war on Iran has already cost Europeans more than 100 billion euros ($112bn).

* The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (Ocha) reports that the number of settler attacks in the West Bank affecting the olive harvest season has already exceeded last year’s number.

* Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz and senior military, police ​and prison officials have been placed under investigation in Italy over the treatment of Gaza flotilla ‌activists, Italian prosecutors said on Friday.

item.title: [World news | The Guardian] Plan to make firms pay more to train older workers than youth apprentices in England
item.description:
Exclusive: Ministers considering overhaul of apprenticeship funding scheme to tackle youth jobs crisis

Employers in England are to be forced to pay more to train an older worker than a youth apprentice under plans being drawn up by the government to tackle the youth jobs crisis.

The Guardian understands ministers plan to overhaul Labour’s apprenticeship funding scheme to increase the cost of training by 25% for a worker over the age of 25 in order to encourage businesses to train young people instead.

item.title: [World news | The Guardian] ‘I cannot carry all of this alone’: the couples kept apart by the war in Gaza
item.description:
Families have been scattered, fathers separated from their children, and couples unable to reunite and marry

Wijdan Abu Matar, 43, was forced to leave Gaza in November 2023 with her eight children for medical treatment, while her injured husband, Hatem, remained behind.

Wijdan and her family were living in the Nuseirat refugee camp when the Gaza war began with the 7 October 2023 Hamas attack on Israel. Ten days later, on 17 October that year, an Israeli strike hit the al-Muhandseen tower, near their home, injuring Wijdan and every member of her family.
